feature_classes.definition: The global envelope and principal shape of one completed part, not a substitute for local semantic-feature coverage.

includes: Overall envelope, principal axes or planes, and dominant external form.
excludes: Local holes, slots, transitions, and manufacturing contexts.

feature_classes.definition: A local positive, negative, transition, wall, or surface form with independent drawing-expression significance.

includes: Local forms that affect manufacture, assembly, function, or inspection.
excludes: Pure relationships and stock-process context.

feature_classes.definition: A concrete global envelope dominated by principal planar faces, including plate-like and prismatic single parts.

includes: Plate-like and prismatic completed-part envelopes with stable principal planes.
excludes: Local holes, slots, transitions, and independent positive structures.

feature_classes.definition: A standard, functional, or process-specific mechanical structure whose semantics exceed raw B-Rep shape.

includes: Threads, transmission forms, springs, conduits, weld preparations, and formed sheet structures.
excludes: Unqualified primitive holes, slots, and transitions.

feature_classes.definition: A relationship among semantic features or occurrences that creates an independent expression obligation.

includes: Patterns, symmetry, mirrors, coaxiality, and geometric intersections.
excludes: The individual related feature shapes.

feature_classes.definition: A controlled manufacturing or stock context that changes drawing rules without becoming a geometric feature itself.

includes: Cast, forged, molded, welded, machined, and formed-sheet contexts.
excludes: Geometry inferred only from appearance without a controlled source.

feature_classes.definition: A round or otherwise explicitly typed negative feature organized around an axis and one or more openings.

includes: Through, blind, counterbored, countersunk, stepped, tapered, oblique, and intersecting holes.
excludes: Obround slots and arbitrary pockets.

feature_classes.definition: A hole whose cylindrical or typed passage intersects two external openings.

includes: Simple through passages with two proven external openings.
excludes: Blind holes and open-ended slots.

feature_classes.definition: A one-opening axial hole with a controlled cylindrical depth and an explicitly classified bottom form.

includes: Blind drilled holes with flat, conical drill-point, spherical, or otherwise typed bottoms.
excludes: Blind pockets without a hole axis.

feature_classes.definition: A semantically grouped coaxial or otherwise controlled multi-level hole such as a stepped, counterbored, or countersunk hole.

includes: Counterbores, countersinks, spotfaces, and multi-diameter stepped holes.
excludes: Unrelated holes that only happen to be near one another.

feature_classes.definition: A hole whose spatial direction or controlled intersection cannot generally be proven by one principal projection.

includes: Oblique entries, radial holes, and controlled intersections between passages.
excludes: Principal-axis holes fully determined by one direct opening view and one section.

feature_classes.definition: An elongated or section-defined negative feature with controlled width, path, end form, and extent.

includes: Straight, open, obround, key, annular, relief, T, dovetail, sealing, and lubrication grooves.
excludes: Round holes and unrestricted pockets.

feature_classes.definition: A slot with two end arcs or semicircles and a controlled center path, treated as a slot rather than a hole.

includes: Through or blind obround slots with explicit end geometry.
excludes: Circular holes and arbitrary rounded pockets.

feature_classes.definition: A slot whose manufacturing form requires a true cross-section, including T and dovetail slots.

includes: T-slots, dovetail slots, and other non-rectangular controlled slot sections.
excludes: Straight rectangular slots fully defined in a direct view.

feature_classes.definition: A groove open to an exterior boundary whose true end profile and longitudinal extent are independently significant.

includes: Longitudinal semicylindrical, V, U, and other typed exterior-opening grooves.
excludes: Closed pockets, circular holes, and section-defined undercut slots such as T-slots.

feature_classes.definition: A bounded negative volume with a controlled opening, floor or through state, wall profile, and location.

includes: Machined pockets and local cavities with explicit boundary and depth.
excludes: Global shell interiors and typed holes or slots.

feature_classes.definition: A local material-adding or retained structure with independent size and location significance.

includes: Bosses, hubs, lugs, feet, ribs, and local pads.
excludes: The undifferentiated overall body envelope.

feature_classes.definition: A typed local positive structure whose subtype and dependent holes or slots remain explicitly recorded.

includes: Bosses, hubs, lugs, ears, mounting feet, and pads.
excludes: Ribs and global flanges.

feature_classes.definition: A thin load-carrying or stiffening positive feature with special longitudinal-section drawing treatment.

includes: Ribs, webs, spokes, and gussets when represented as semantic stiffeners.
excludes: General thin walls and unrelated plates.

feature_classes.definition: A controlled change in level, diameter, width, or axial extent between adjacent regions.

includes: Axial steps, shoulders, registers, and flange levels.
excludes: Uncontrolled transition faces and cosmetic edges.

feature_classes.definition: A paired or bounded wall structure whose thickness and inner/outer profile require coordinated expression.

includes: Uniform or locally varying walls and shell cavities.
excludes: Independent ribs and ordinary solid-body faces.

feature_classes.definition: A local edge transition represented once as a semantic feature even when it produces multiple B-Rep faces.

includes: Chamfers, rounds, blend surfaces, and controlled relief transitions.
excludes: Theoretical sharp intersections that are not modelled transitions.

labels.zh_cn: 斜面、锥面、球面或自由曲面
labels.en: inclined, conical, spherical, or free-form surface

feature_classes.definition: A surface whose true form, axis, center, or controlled data reference may require an auxiliary or sectional expression.

includes: Inclined planes, cones, spheres, and controlled free-form surfaces.
excludes: Ordinary principal planes and cylinders already represented by another typed feature.

feature_classes.definition: An internal or external thread whose standard, size, pitch, class, hand, and effective extent require controlled feature data or PMI.

includes: Internal, external, straight, tapered, pipe, multi-start, and left-hand threads.
excludes: Unqualified cosmetic helical geometry without controlled thread semantics.

feature_classes.definition: A gear, spline, worm, rack, sprocket, pulley, timing-tooth, ratchet, or cam structure requiring controlled product semantics.

includes: Gears, splines, worms, racks, sprockets, pulleys, timing forms, ratchets, and cams.
excludes: Decorative repeated serrations without a transmission function.

feature_classes.definition: A bend, flange, hem, bead, louver, formed hole, or other controlled sheet-metal form.

includes: Bends, flanges, hems, beads, louvers, formed holes, and local sheet forms.
excludes: Flat machined plates without a controlled sheet-forming context.

feature_classes.definition: A compression, extension, torsion, disc, or other spring requiring type-specific controlled parameters.

includes: Compression, extension, torsion, disc, and typed special springs.
excludes: Unqualified helical decorations and flexible hoses.

feature_classes.definition: A bent tube, port network, oil passage, or internal flow path whose route and intersections require explicit expression.

includes: Bent tubes, ports, oilways, and intersecting internal passage networks.
excludes: A single ordinary hole without flow-path semantics.

feature_classes.definition: A controlled weld preparation or post-weld machined structure, without treating an assembly weldment as a single-part model by default.

includes: Groove preparations and post-weld machining features on an in-scope single part.
excludes: Assembly drawing weld definitions and unsupported multi-body weldments.

feature_classes.definition: A linear, rectangular, circular, path-based, or unequal repetition with explicit seed and actual occurrences.

includes: Patterns with seed, occurrence IDs, count, spacing or spread, and suppression state.
excludes: Coincidentally similar independent features without a proven grouping.

feature_classes.definition: A proven symmetry or mirror relationship with a frozen axis or plane and explicit exceptions.

includes: Exact geometric symmetry and feature-tree mirror relationships.
excludes: Nearly symmetric geometry or sides with unrecorded differences.

feature_classes.definition: A deterministic axis-to-axis or path intersection relationship among semantic features.

includes: Coaxial levels, intersecting holes, and connected flow passages.
excludes: Functional geometric tolerances not present in controlled PMI.

feature_classes.definition: A controlled cast-stock context with casting-specific draft, parting, allowance, radius, and defect requirements.

includes: Parts explicitly identified as cast stock by a controlled source.
excludes: Forgings and geometry merely resembling a casting.

feature_classes.definition: A controlled forged-stock context kept distinct from casting rules and evidence.

includes: Parts explicitly identified as forged stock by a controlled source.
excludes: Cast or molded stock and geometry inferred only from appearance.

feature_classes.definition: A controlled molded-part context with mold-specific parting, draft, wall, and local-form rules.

includes: Parts explicitly identified as molded by a controlled source.
excludes: Cast, forged, or machined parts inferred from appearance.
